- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 79.16 or 79.68), then corrects with a downward bias.
- Underestimates in the middle-to-late horizon (days 15–30) when true values show upward momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices will return to prior levels too quickly, missing sustained upward trends.
- Lagged response: model reacts to recent history with delay — e.g., 79.58 → 80.08 is forecasted too early, while true peak is delayed.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts show persistent overestimation, especially when history includes recent volatility or spikes.
- Avoid extrapolating from recent high volatility — model tends to overreact to short-term noise.
